topic.title: After You Suggest Changes
topic.shortdesc: A review task created by a Contributor has no owner until a project maintainer or owner takes it over and drives it to completion.

body.p: Usually, the user who creates a review task becomes its owner. This is not the case for a task created by a Contributor: the task is created without an owner, because a Contributor cannot integrate changes into a project. The task waits for someone who can.

section.title: What Happens to Your Task

ol.li: Everyone who can own the review tasks of the project, meaning its maintainers and owners, receives an email notification telling them that you created a task that needs an owner.
One of them opens the task and clicks Assign Me as Owner. From that moment, they own the task and manage the review.
You receive an email notification that tells you who took the task over.
The new owner runs the review, and can integrate the accepted changes into the project.

section.p: Until someone takes the task, it stays in the project's list of review tasks with no owner listed. If nobody takes it, contact a project maintainer or owner directly.

section.title: Your Role in the Task
section.p: You take part in the task you created as a Reviewer. The task remains in your list of review tasks, and you can keep editing the files in it, answer the questions of the other participants, and follow the discussion.
Only the owner of the task can manage it: change its settings, share it with other users, close the review, and integrate the changes.
